finding.claim: Root CA and intermediate CA private keys are written to disk as unencrypted PFX files (no password) with default file permissions, in a directory shared across applications; the leaf key PEM is also written unencrypted with default permissions (lines 77, 99-100).
finding.source: Precondition only, not attacker-controlled input: non-CF host (Platform.IsCloudFoundry false) where the app calls AddAppInstanceIdentityCertificate.
finding.sink: File.WriteAllBytes(RootCaPfxPath, caCertificate.Export(X509ContentType.Pfx)) at LocalCertificateWriter.cs:62; intermediate at :77; File.WriteAllText of leaf key at :100.

trace.note: Platform.IsCloudFoundry gate; non-CF path runs writer
ParentPath = parent of app base dir
root CA exported as PFX with private key, no password, no file mode set
intermediate CA exported the same way
CF_SYSTEM_CERT_PATH set to the same directory, so consumers trust this root

finding.guards_checked: Platform gate (only skips on real CF); existence check at :59/:74 prevents overwrite but not disclosure; no password on export; no file-mode or ACL set; no encryption. None protect the key material. Impact: any local user or process that can read ParentPath can take the root CA key (valid to 2039, :112) and mint instance-identity certs with arbitrary OU org/space/app values (format at :48). Also a TOCTOU race between exists-check and write when processes start together.

finding.claim: Password masking only matches 'password=' at start-of-string or after ';', so comma-delimited Redis-style connection strings leak their password through /actuator/env when stored under a non-default key.
finding.source: Config value of the form 'host:port,password=...' stored under a key that does not match default KeysToSanitize (ConfigureEnvironmentEndpointOptions.cs:13-22). Requires env endpoint to be exposed (default exposure is health,info).
finding.sink: Response body of the env endpoint via EnvironmentEndpointHandler.cs:84-88.

trace.note: sanitizer obtained and applied to each value
key-based match returns ****** when key matches
value-based password masking; ',password=' not matched, value returned unmasked

finding.guards_checked: Key-based matchers (default keys include password$, .*connectionstring.*, .*credentials.*, vcap_services); URI userinfo masking (Sanitizer.cs:56); endpoint exposure gating (EndpointOptionsExtensions.cs:21-42). Standard Redis keys are masked by key name; bypass requires a non-default key name and exposed env endpoint.

finding.claim: Heap dump is written to a predictable timestamp-only filename in the shared temp directory and served from there, with no random component or permission control.
finding.source: Local access on a multi-user host (Linux /tmp is shared; macOS TMPDIR is per-user) plus permission to trigger the dump.
finding.sink: client.WriteDump(...) at HeapDumper.cs:131 (and GCHeapDump.WriteMemoryGraph at :106) writing to outputPath.
finding.guards_checked: Path.GetFullPath normalizes but does not stop symlinks; File.Exists before streaming; delete in finally. No O_EXCL, no random suffix, no restricted file mode. Thread dump uses GetRandomFileName (EventPipeThreadDumper.cs:169) and is not affected.

finding.claim: The _links response builds hrefs from the unvalidated X-Forwarded-Proto header and the Host header, so the requester can get attacker-chosen link URLs.
finding.sink: Link.Href values in the JSON _links response built in HypermediaService.cs:98-116.

trace.note: scheme taken from X-Forwarded-Proto with no allowlist

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist on scheme or host. Exposure and enable checks govern which links are listed, not their values. Real impact needs a shared cache that stores /actuator responses without keying on Host or X-Forwarded-Proto, or a client that renders the links.
